analysis.title: Lord of GPUs: The Return of the King (2026)
key_insights: Nvidia's Board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang, citing satisfaction with his candor and input from senior US government levels that his return poses no national security risk.
Wedbush sees US administration preferences as a factor: President Trump advocated for Jensen's return and Scott Bessent called him an 'outsider', meeting his prior preferred criteria.
Arm CEO Rene Haas, seen as the most likely external candidate, committed to Arm through 2033 as of the morning of the announcement.
The reinstatement likely preserves NVDA policies such as startup and data center financing and supply chain support, and keeps NVDA as an AI industry advocate with high-level government access.

Open questions are whether the US will minimize its apparent investigation into NVDA's accounting practices (circular investments, illicit GPU shipments) and moderate new Asian chip export and Chinese data center rules.
Wedbush believes these two issues weighed on sentiment the past week and sees milder resolution as more probable with Jensen's return.
If AI trade concerns ease, Wedbush expects memory, HDDs and optics to be the biggest winners, having underperformed badly and now trading well below typical peak-cycle valuations.
Channel checks through last week suggest AI is operating business as usual with supply, not demand, the main constraint, and GPU rental pricing continues to rise.
Wedbush sees US policy as a greater risk than financing and views administration support for Jensen as shifting the policy risk profile favorably. Rating stays Outperform.
Valuation: PT unchanged at $293 on ~17.5X FY28 EPS estimate of $16.59 (raised from $15.53) plus net cash of $2.70/share. Stock at $125.53.

market_movers.rationale: Jensen Huang's reinstatement and administration support lower forward US policy risk while AI demand remains supply constrained.

sector_views.rationale: Supply remains the constraint on AI demand and policy risk may ease.
These would be the greatest winners if AI concerns moderate, given depressed valuations and better odds forward pricing and margins hold.

earnings_insights: Wedbush FY2028 EPS estimate for NVDA (estimate, not reported) raised to $16.59 from $15.53.
PT based on ~17.5X PE on FY28 EPS estimate of $16.59 plus net cash of $2.70/share.
risk_factors: Uncertainty over how Jensen's reinstatement affects internal company dynamics.
US investigation into NVDA accounting practices could hit AI investments and supplier/customer relationships.
Tighter US chip export rules and restrictions on Chinese data center use.
AI demand deterioration or data center customer investment softening, or capital constraints.
Competition from AMD and INTC, and customers shifting to internal silicon.
Acquisitions, product misexecution, weak gaming demand, and West-China tensions disrupting supply chain.
geopolitical: US government reportedly investigating NVDA's accounting practices, with focus possibly on circular investments or illicit GPU shipments.
New US regulations on Asian chip exports and restrictions on Chinese companies using data centers outside China have weighed on sentiment.
Tensions between the West and China are listed as a risk to NVDA's China share and supply chain.
